title: Instagram Story Ad Images with Square Photos | AIVideosUGC
description: Turn one product photo into a square Instagram Story ad image with room for a headline and price. Place that square on a tall 9:16 phone frame after download.
h1: Instagram Story Ad Images from a Square Product Photo
lead: A feed crop often cuts the product and leaves no room for the offer. Upload one photo and get Instagram story ad images composed for a Story layout.
steps_h2: How to Make a Square Story Image in 3 Simple Steps
steps_lead: Upload the product, describe a simple setting, then place the square photo in your Story layout.

steps.d: Show one complete product with open space around it. A plain or simple background is enough when the product itself is clear.
Name the surface, where the light comes from, and one extra object. Keep the product as the subject so there is room for text.
Place the square download on a tall 9:16 frame and add the price, date, and button there. Check the phone view before you post.

faq.q: Can the Story image include my price or code?
faq.a: Add the price, code and button after download in your design or ads tool. The generated image has no text, so you can change a digit without making the image again.

faq.q: Does the template output a 9:16 file?
faq.a: No. You get a square photo, laid out for a Story. 9:16 is the tall phone shape. Place the square on that frame in your editor, then add the text.

faq.q: Why not crop a feed photo into a Story?
faq.a: A crop can cut off the product and leave no room for a headline. This scene keeps the full item centered, with open space away from the header and the lower button.

faq.q: Can I use the same image in Facebook Stories and in the feed?
faq.a: Yes. The square file can go in an Instagram Story layout, a Facebook Story layout, a feed post, a carousel or a listing.

faq.q: When should I use a tall video instead?
faq.a: Use video when the product needs to move. This template is the photo. Tall video ads start at [creator-style video ads](page:video-ads).

faq.q: What does a Story photo cost?
faq.a: Each photo costs 24 credits. The cost is shown before you start, and a failed run puts those credits back. The download has no watermark, and you can use it in your own ads, pages, and posts.

faq.q: Will the full product stay visible?
faq.a: Check the edges against your source photo before you post. The layout leaves space around the product, but it does not keep every edge exactly as shot.

faq.q: Can I ask for a hand or a person in the scene?
faq.a: Yes. Describe one hand or one adult action while the uploaded product stays the subject. The person is generated, not a hired creator.

faq.q: Who are Instagram story ad images for?
faq.a: Beauty and skincare shops, and other product sellers who need the item fully in frame with room for a headline. Upload one photo and download the square.

faq.q: Can a beginner make a Story image?
faq.a: Yes. Upload one product photo, name a simple setting, and download the square. Add the price and button in your editor after that.

faq.q: Can I start from a product link and a script?
faq.a: Yes. Paste the product page or a short brief, edit the drafted line, and keep this square as the Story frame.

faq.q: Can I publish the Story to Instagram or TikTok?
faq.a: Yes. Place the square on a tall 9:16 frame, add a spoken line if you want one, and publish to Instagram, Facebook, or TikTok.
